title: Hearing on coordinating city services for older adults
summary: The Council's Committee on Aging held an oversight hearing on how city agencies, especially the Department for the Aging, coordinate services for older New Yorkers through the Cabinet for Older New Yorkers. The committee also heard a bill (Int. 230) that would create a financial assistance program of up to $10,000 per person to help low-income older adults and people with disabilities install home safety features like grab bars and stair lifts, and a resolution (Res. 373) urging Albany to pass a state long-term care trust program. New York City's population aged 65 and older grew about 53% between 2000 and 2023.
